name: Leg press
cue: Go deep; stop before your tailbone lifts.
research: v10 (science audit A1, 4 Oct 2026): depth. The back pad is reclined to 15 deg above horizontal (trunk -75; v9 30 deg, trunk -60) on the 45 deg sled with the plate square to the rails, so the closed chain is hip - knee + ankle = 45 + 15 = 60 in every pose (v9: 75) and each degree of recline buys a degree of knee bend. Feet mid-plate (the plate is centred on the mid-soles). Depth: hip 120 / knee 95 / ankle 35 (v9 119 / 71 / 27): the knees bend about 90-100 deg (Larsen 2025: stopping at 100 deg on a 45 deg sled grew the quads as much as going to 154 deg; deeper squats grew the glutes and adductors more, Kubo 2019) while the pelvis stays flat on the pad (hip under the rig's 122 cap, where real lifters start to tuck the pelvis). The ankle reaches the weight-bearing dorsiflexion of a loaded lunge (rig cap raised from the non-weight-bearing 28 to 35: Hall & Docherty 2017 measured 39-45 deg and call under 30 restricted). Cue: "Go deep; stop before your tailbone lifts." (the depth limit is the pelvis tucking, i.e. the lower back rounding off the pad). Lockout: knee 12 with the hip (72.97) solved so the mid-soles travel on the 45 deg rail line; ankle -0.97; sled travel 0.29 m. Stance (audit A1): heels about 45 cm apart, toes out 18 deg, knees over the toes: at depth the hip abducts 26 and turns out 6 (the knee tracks ~14 deg out on the plate) and the foot IK sets the toes to 18 (a 7 deg tibial rotation at 95 deg of knee flexion); at lockout the hip (abduction 11.1, rotation 16.12) keeps the mid-soles on the same plate sockets (x +-0.144 H) with the toes already at 18, so the straight knee carries no twist. The whole seat unit (back pad, headrest, seat pan rising 27 deg toward the front, side handles) is the v9 unit turned 15 deg about the hip-joint centre with the pelvis, so the back, sacrum, sit bones, head and hands keep their v9 contacts; the arms are the v9 arms (handles on the pad frame level with the front of the pelvis, forearms clear of the working glutes and quads). Soles held flat on the sliding plate by foot IK. The skin is bound at the stretched pose (motion.bind 0.074 s into the press), which paints the glute and vastus lateralis footprints so they meet in a broad band at every hip angle. Muscles: glute max and vastus lateralis (the vastus medialis faces away on the near leg; the adductor magnus is hidden from the side camera; rectus femoris, slack at this hip flexion, stays dark). Geometry: tools/design/leg_press_v10.mjs (v9: tools/design/leg_press.mjs). Load: plate horns on the sled carriage (the plates ride up the rails with the sled; tools/design/loads.mjs).

targets.note: v10 depth (science audit A1): pad 15 deg above horizontal, closed chain hip - knee + ankle = 60; bottom 120 / 95 / 35, lockout knee 12 with the hip solved on the rail line

camera.note: Research view az 90 / el 10, unchanged: the glutes and vasti face the side camera at every phase, and the horizon arc stays visible between the floor skids.

right sole stays flat on the sled plate
sit bones stay on the seat pan
